courseTitle: Vue - The Complete Guide (incl. Router & Composition API)

cues.en: So that's it for the module.
And this was a huge course section.
Of course, since we covered all the important fundamentals you need to know about view, we learned
how interacting with the DOM works and how View manages templates to allow you to use certain view features
which are then reflected on the actual page.
You'll learn that view has this core idea of letting you define the goal rather than the individual
steps, so that it follows that declarative approach where you define how your page should look like
and which parts on the page might be dynamic, and you let then view figure out how to get there.
Now, in order to let View do its job, you need to connect your view app your view instance to the
actual HTML code with the Mount method which you saw.
Then you can use a CSS selector to select a part of the page and turn that part into the template of
the View app in which you then can use all these view features.
Like for example, the data and event binding features you'll learn about.
You'll learn that data can be output in that template.
So in the controlled HTML code, by using the double curly brace syntax for this interpolation syntax
to just output some text which might change over time in a certain place of the page or with the V bind
directive to bind HTML attributes to some dynamic value.
You also learn about this shorthand notation where instead of V bind colon some attribute, you just
have colon some attribute to then bind that attribute to a dynamic value.
And we, of course, cannot just output data.
We can also listen to events with the V on directive or the at shorthand notation.
Now, these are the powerful core features Vue is all about.
But in order to make these features really powerful and to make them more useful, we rely on vue's
built in reactivity system.
That simply means that Vue will update the real DOM whenever some data which you're outputting with
V bind or double curly braces changes and you learn that you can register data which might change in
the data option of your Vue app and that you can also work with computed properties and watchers to
calculate results dynamically or to run some code.
Whenever some data changes and Vue watches the data for you, it automatically detects changes for you
and it will update the DOM and therefore what the user sees on the page whenever such changes are detected.
Now that's the important foundation you need when working with Vue, but it's of course not just about
outputting text or data in web apps.
We also, of course want to make them look pretty and that involves styling.
And here Vue also can help us with achieving dynamic styling because we can, of course, all the sets
see us as classes or inline styles dynamically with V Bind.
And you also learned that Vue has special syntax for classes and inline styles to help you assign dynamic
styles to make that easier for you with that object or erase syntax I covered over the last lectures.
Now that's the foundation.
It's of course, not all you need to know, but it's the foundation for the rest of the course, and
you will see the concepts taught in this course section throughout all our course sections.
So make sure you understand this.
Go through the lectures, which might not be clear to you at this point, and do the challenge as an
exercise, as I offer to you in the section, so that you really know what these core concepts are all
about.
